title: Streaming Sticks and OLED TVs 2026: What to Buy, From £9.95 | Megastore76
metaDescription: A £9.95 streaming stick will make an old TV feel new. Ten sticks from £9.95 to £59.95 compared, plus the two OLEDs — and honest notes on the listings whose pictures print a price the store does not charge.
h1: Your TV is probably fine — the £9.95 stick is what makes it feel new
intro: Most people shopping for a television do not need a television. They need the £9.95 stick that gives the one they already own 4K streaming, a voice remote and every app — without a new screen, a new wall bracket, or a new delivery to arrange. This page compares ten streaming sticks from £9.95 to £59.95 and the two OLEDs at the top of the range, with the catch on each one stated rather than buried.
updated: Every price on this page was checked against the Megastore76 store on 29 September 2026.
chips: Honest note on the listing pictures

verdict.heading: Three answers, depending on the question you are actually asking
verdict.intro: If the screen is fine and you just want the apps, spend £9.95 and stop reading. If you want the one that lasts and handles a busy home network, go to the Wi-Fi 6 stick at £59.95. If you are genuinely replacing the television, that is a different purchase entirely and it starts at £1,499.

products.name: Amazon Fire Stick TV 4K
products.summary: This is the product that makes the rest of the page unnecessary for most people. £9.95 buys 4K Ultra HD streaming and a voice control remote, and it plugs into any television with an HDMI port. If your existing TV works perfectly well but its built-in smart menu has become slow, this replaces that menu entirely for the price of a takeaway. There is no clever catch here — it is simply the cheapest way to modernise a screen you already own.

guide.heading: Five things that decide whether you will be happy with it
guide.intro: A streaming stick is a simple purchase, but there are two specifications that people get wrong and one that costs them money for nothing.

points.h: Check the resolution before the price
points.p: This is the mistake on this page. The Roku Streaming Stick 2025 is HD only, and it costs £28.99 — nearly three times the £9.95 stick, which does 4K. If your television is 4K, buying an HD stick means paying more to use less of your screen. Read the resolution column in the table above before you look at any price.

points.h: Wi-Fi 6 is the only spec worth paying a premium for
points.p: Everything a streaming stick does happens over your network, so the network is the real bottleneck. On a crowded home network an older stick will quietly drop resolution or buffer, and no amount of processor speed fixes that. Wi-Fi 6 — the 4K Plus at £34.89 and the 4K Max at £59.95 — is what actually prevents it.

points.h: You are choosing an interface, and a shop
points.p: Fire TV puts Amazon's content in front of you and comes from Amazon's app store. Roku is neutral and puts your apps first. Android TV is Google's. None is wrong, but you will look at this every day, so pick the one that suits how you watch rather than the one that is cheapest by a pound.

points.h: A stick is not an upgrade to your picture
points.p: It is worth being clear about what you are buying. A stick changes what your television can play, and how easily you find it. It does not improve contrast, brightness or motion. If your complaint is that the picture looks flat or grey, no stick will fix it — that is a new panel, which is the £1,499 conversation at the bottom of this page.

points.h: Ask why there are two picks at £39.99
points.p: There are two products at exactly £39.99 here — the Fire TV 4K Select, which is the current generation, and a plain 4K Streaming Stick. They are not the same product and we have not pretended they are: the Fire TV listing tells you more about what you are getting, and the other one has a clean product image. Pick on which of those matters more to you.

faqHeading: Common questions about streaming sticks and TVs

faq.q: Do I actually need a new TV, or just a streaming stick?
faq.a: If your screen works and you simply want the apps, a stick. The £9.95 Fire Stick adds 4K streaming and a voice remote to any television with an HDMI port. Replace the television only when the picture itself is the complaint — contrast, brightness, motion — because a stick cannot change any of those.

faq.q: What is the difference between HD and 4K on a streaming stick?
faq.a: 4K is roughly four times the resolution of HD. If you own a 4K television you need a 4K stick to use it, otherwise you are paying for a screen you are not filling. One product on this page — the Roku Streaming Stick 2025 at £28.99 — is HD only, and it is more expensive than the 4K stick at £9.95.

faq.q: Is Wi-Fi 6 worth the extra money on a Fire TV Stick?
faq.a: It is worth it if your home network is busy or your television is far from the router. Wi-Fi 6 handles many connected devices at once far better than standard Wi-Fi, which is what stops 4K buffering when other people in the house are streaming or gaming. If you live alone with the TV near the router, standard Wi-Fi is fine.

faq.q: Why is one of these products unboxed?
faq.a: The Fire Stick TV 4K 1st Gen at £38.50 is listed as unboxed and first generation. That means older hardware than the £39.99 current-generation stick — which is a penny more. Unless that specific saving matters to you, the current generation at the same price is the better buy.

faq.q: Why are most of the listing pictures missing from this page?
faq.a: Because several of them print a price the store does not charge — some advertise a figure well below what the product actually costs. Putting an image like that next to the real price invites a customer to read one number, pay another, and feel misled. So those images are left off the page and the products are described in full instead. Where a listing has a second image with no price on it at all, that is the one we use.

That depends entirely on what you are comparing it to. Against a mid-range LED television, OLED's self-lit pixels give you true black, which is the single most visible improvement in picture quality available. Against the £9.95 stick on a television you already own, it is a completely different purchase. Buy it because you want a better screen, not because you want the apps.

faq.q: Will a streaming stick work with an old TV?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the television has an HDMI port — which covers essentially anything made in the last fifteen years. The stick does the work; the television is just the display. This is why a stick is normally the better buy than replacing a working screen.
